attributes.description: Fires when the backends PostgreSQL reports approach the max_connections ceiling set by the compute tier. Connection exhaustion is the single most common way a Supabase project fails: once the ceiling is reached, new clients are refused outright. Utilisation is measured from pg_stat_database_num_backends rather than the pooler-reported counts, because that is the number PostgreSQL enforces the ceiling against and it is the only one that also includes direct clients, the exporter and platform utilities.
attributes.name: [Supabase OTel] PostgreSQL connection budget nearly exhausted

investigation_guide.blob:
## PostgreSQL Connection Budget Nearly Exhausted

`max_connections` is a hard, small, tier-fixed budget. Supavisor, PgBouncer, PostgREST and GoTrue all draw from it, and clients can connect directly as well. When it runs out, new connections are refused rather than queued.

### Interpreting the columns
`Backends` drives the alert and is PostgreSQL's own count. `Pooled Connections` and `Direct Connections` are what the poolers report and will total slightly lower, because neither sees the exporter or the platform utilities. A large gap between `Backends` and the two together means something outside the poolers is holding connections.

### Triage Steps
1. Read the `Direct Connections` column on the alert. A high direct count means clients are bypassing the pooler and eating the budget the poolers need — that is an application anti-pattern, not a capacity problem.
2. Identify which role holds the connections: `TS metrics-supabase.metrics.otel-* | STATS conns = MAX(LAST_OVER_TIME(connection_stats_connection_count)) BY attributes.username | SORT conns DESC`
3. Do not reach for a larger pool first. The usual root cause is queries running slower than they should, so connections are held longer. Check disk IO utilisation, mean query time, and long-running transactions before resizing anything.
4. Check for a long-running transaction pinning a backend: `pg_stat_activity_xact_runtime`.

### Tuning
Supabase guidance is to leave the poolers no more than ~40% of `max_connections` when the PostgREST API is in heavy use (up to ~80% otherwise), so the remainder stays free for Auth and platform utilities. Utilisation is therefore meaningful well before 100% — lower the 90% threshold to 70-80% if you want earlier warning.

### Related content
Connection headroom is deliberately not tracked as an SLO: a pool can sit fully checked out and still be healthy provided nothing queues behind it, so a headroom budget would burn without user impact. This rule is the only connection-budget signal. `pgbouncer_pools_client_waiting_connections` and `pgrst_db_pool_waiting` rise during the same incident and are left as dashboard context rather than duplicated as rules.
